initial_requirements: Qheadache is intended to be a standalone computerized puzzle game for people ranging from young beginners to adult players. Players use a graphical board to move blocks and solve a predefined challenge. The application should support normal play and retain useful information about a player's progress and results, such as time, actions, and scores.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary success goals for Qheadache—for example, the main player experience, educational or entertainment outcomes, and any business or usage goals you want the game to achieve?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main goal is to give players a smooth, enjoyable puzzle experience that feels easy to pick up but still satisfying to solve. We want it to work well for beginners and also stay interesting for adults, so the game should be both entertaining and mentally engaging.
From a usage standpoint, success would mean players can complete puzzles without confusion, understand their progress clearly, and want to keep replaying or improving their times and scores. We are not really aiming for a business-heavy product here, more for a solid standalone game that people actually enjoy using and returning to.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Who are the key stakeholders involved in Qheadache, and what responsibilities or interests does each group have (for example, players, game designers, administrators, or anyone else who will use, manage, or support the game)?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The key stakeholders are mainly the players, since they’re the ones using the game and caring about the puzzle experience, progress, and scores. Then there are the game designers or content owners, who care about the puzzle challenges themselves and whether the gameplay feels balanced and engaging.
We’d also have an administrator or support person if needed, mostly to manage the game setup, review progress data, or handle updates and issues. I’m not sure yet if we need any separate technical support role beyond that, but those are the main groups I’d expect.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What kinds of configuration or content-management capabilities should Qheadache provide for the administrator or support person—for example, what puzzle settings, challenge definitions, difficulty tuning, data management, or update controls need to be configurable, and how should those changes be applied?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
At a minimum, the administrator should be able to set up or change the puzzles that are available, including the board layout and the predefined challenge the player has to solve. It would also be useful to adjust difficulty-related things like how hard a puzzle is or which challenges are shown to beginners versus more advanced players.
For data management, I’d expect access to player results and progress records, maybe with the ability to clear or archive them if needed. As for updates, I think changes should be applied centrally and then take effect the next time the game starts, unless it’s a very small setting change that can safely be applied immediately.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Provide a smooth, enjoyable puzzle experience that is easy to pick up, satisfying to solve, works well for beginners while remaining interesting for adults, and encourages replaying to improve times and scores.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Players use the game and care about the puzzle experience, progress, and scores; game designers/content owners define and balance puzzle challenges; an administrator or support person manages game setup, reviews progress data, and handles updates or issues.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Support normal gameplay on a graphical board where players move blocks to solve a predefined challenge; show clear progress; record player results such as time, actions, and scores; allow an administrator to configure available puzzles, board layouts, challenge definitions, difficulty settings, and player progress/result data management.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Puzzle difficulty and availability should be configurable so beginner and advanced challenges can be separated; player progress and results should be retained for tracking time, actions, and scores; administrative changes are generally applied centrally and may take effect on the next game start unless the change is small enough to apply immediately.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Puzzle definitions, board layouts, predefined challenges, player progress records, player result records, time measurements, action counts, and scores.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Standalone computerized puzzle game; configuration changes are typically applied centrally; some updates take effect only when the game is restarted; intended for a broad audience from young beginners to adults.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: The game should be easy to pick up, provide clear progress understanding, feel smooth and enjoyable, and remain satisfying and mentally engaging.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: If updates are not small enough to apply immediately, they should take effect the next time the game starts.

slots.name: configuration_management
slots.value: Administrators should be able to set or change available puzzles, board layouts, predefined challenges, and difficulty-related settings; changes should be managed centrally and usually applied on the next game start, with minor safe settings allowed to apply immediately.

slots.name: progress_data_retention_policy
slots.value: Player results and progress records should be retained; administrators should be able to review them and optionally clear or archive them if needed.

slots.name: admin_support_capabilities
slots.value: Manage game setup, configure available puzzles and challenge definitions, adjust difficulty, review player progress and results, and clear or archive progress data when needed.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The stakeholder list includes an administrator or support person to manage game setup, review progress data, and handle updates/issues, even though the product is described as a standalone puzzle game rather than a service with heavy operational needs.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This suggests there may be an implicit need for configurable content, local management of player/progress data, and controlled release or maintenance workflows so the game can be operated, tuned, and supported without requiring players to interact with technical details.
